what: Per-work capture status for MIGNE'S OWN numbered conjecture notes — the foot-of-page apparatus (`Forte *word*.`) that Corpus Corporum's TEI omits entirely. Measured 2026-08-18: zero such notes across all 5,276 PL TEI files and 498,774 <note> elements. See CLAUDE.md.

tiers.2: Text + OUR apparatus (markers, cruces). Migne's conjecture notes NOT captured. This is every work shipped before 2026-08-18 and is the default.
tiers.3: Text + our apparatus + MIGNE'S conjecture notes recovered from the plate, sequence verified unbroken.

coverage_values.partial: some notes captured — typically incidental finds during a targeted plate read. The sequence has NOT been verified, so absence of a note here means nothing.
coverage_values.full: the work's whole numbered sequence was read and verified unbroken; any gap is Migne's own and is documented
coverage_values.spot: 1-2 pages of THIS work read at the plate and no foot-of-page apparatus found. A sample, not a proof: it licenses shipping the work without [cn:] recovery, and it does NOT license a claim that the work has no notes. Introduced 2026-08-19 when the spot check became part of chunking, because the alternative in practice was inheriting a zero measured in a different book.
coverage_values.asterisk_layer: Migne's SECOND foot-of-page layer, keyed by a raised asterisk rather than by a number: editorial cross-references, not textual conjectures. Corpus Corporum carries it no more than it carries the numbered one. Ruled 2026-08-24 (Wilson): recover it into the Latin as [cn: * | …] with the numbered notes at chunking, and give it a TRANSLATED [nt: …] opposite in the English — because unlike 'Forte earum' these notes are sentences that say something, and an English-only reader would otherwise be left with a line he cannot read. A numbered [cn:] stays Latin-only, unchanged.

rule: Do NOT retrofit the completed corpus (Wilson, 2026-08-18) — recover notes for NEW works at chunking time. Shipping new works is the funding lever; retrofits are invisible to a reader. Correctness gates are unaffected by this. | 2026-08-19 (Wilson): the plate spot check is PART OF CHUNKING. Every newly chunked work gets 1 page read at the plate (2 where a work division falls mid-page, since notes sit mid-page there) before it is translated. A checked zero is recorded coverage "spot"; notes found are recovered to <idno>.tsv and the work re-chunked so inject-plate-notes places them. Never inherit a sibling book's zero: PL 113 rests on 19 pages across 4 books and PL 114 on 8, and it is the work in hand that ships.

works.mechanical_handle: ⭐ UNLIKE THE NUMBERED LAYER, OUR TEI CARRIES THE ANCHOR. Corpus Corporum keeps Migne's raised letter (as the ordinal indicator ª) while dropping the note it points to, so the anchors are findable by grep instead of by sampling: `grep -c ª` over src/latin/8950 returns exactly 2, at the two sites above, and 0 across 8967, 9000 and 9001. That is what licenses reading only two plates for the notes themselves rather than all 58.
works.why_not_tier_3: Tier 3 asks for the sequence verified unbroken, and a per-page letter layer HAS no sequence to verify -- so the guarantee tier 3 names cannot be given here, and claiming it would assert a check that was not performed. The evidence actually in hand is the two surviving anchors plus a 10-of-58-page sample; a note whose anchor glyph the digitization dropped would be invisible to both. Recorded as `partial` for that reason: absence of a third note here means nothing.
works.caveat: ⛑ NOTE (a) AT COL 0068B IS RECOVERED BUT NOT PLACED. Its anchor sits INSIDE Migne's own citation -- [n: (BEDA, Hexaem. lib. I, tom. II, col. 13 ª.)] -- and the injector's search view strips [n: …] wholesale, while marker syntax across this corpus forbids nested brackets, so there is no [cn:] position for it that a reader of the marker would survive. It is recorded in data/plate-notes/8950.tsv and reported as skipped on every run rather than being placed by a guess. ⚑ It is also the lower-stakes of the two: it is Migne's EDIT. note explaining that his `col. 13` cross-reference points at the volumes of his own Patrologia. The note at 0094D, which does carry text a reader needs, IS placed.
works.sic_candidate: ⚑ The 0068B note prints `Revocantur lector` -- plural verb, singular subject -- read at 400 dpi with the corners checked first. The same standing note in this volume's Prothemata (a DIFFERENT work, not ours) OCRs as `Revocatur lector`, singular, which would make the Genesis setting a compositor's slip; that plate has NOT been read, so the pair is a lead and not a finding. works.note: FULL SWEEP COMPLETE 2026-09-08. Every leaf of the work read at the foot, both columns, Gallica bpt6k5505319w f92-f148 (57 leaves, cols 0183A-0296C) -- corner numbers confirmed on the six calibration leaves already on file, the letter-class survey run across the rest at ~700px full-page renders (sufficient to distinguish a text block reaching the foot margin from blank paper, which is what this sweep is for) and every leaf reviewed by eye. ONE note found, at f128 (cols 255/256): a raised-letter key 'a' after 'concordia charitatis', an editorial note on the numbering of the Decalogue (Augustine vs Origen). Recovered per Wilson's ruling 2026-09-08 (data/briefs/8949-ADJUDICATIONS.md section 4): the raised letter joins the ASTERISK layer -- [cn: a | ...] on the Latin plus a translated [nt: ...] on the English, since the note is editorial prose and not a bare textual conjecture. The anchor glyph itself was also dropped by Corpus Corporum (0 superscript characters anywhere in the source, unlike 8950 Genesis where the anchor survived); restored by TEI patch (data/tei-patches/8949.json) so inject-plate-notes.mjs places the note by the same machinery as every other letter-keyed work. f129 confirmed clean at its head -- the note does not run over. No numbered conjecture sequence and no second asterisk-layer note anywhere else in the work.

fields.sequence_gaps_documented: Note numbers Migne's own sequence skips, established at the plate. scripts/inject-plate-notes.mjs errors on any gap NOT listed here — a gap is the detector for a page cropped short, so it must be silenced deliberately, one number at a time, and never by widening the check.

findings.what: PL 113's Glossa ordinaria pages carry NO foot-of-page conjecture apparatus on any page sampled.
findings.evidence: Eight pages read at 300 dpi off archive.org patrologiaecurs04migngoog, across three separate runs of the volume: 271-275 (Ruth, incl. the Judges/Ruth division mid-page), 363 and 372 (Nehemiah run), 565 (Ecclesiastes run). Zero numbered notes, and no foot rule of the kind PL 202 prints. The pages simply end.

findings.limit: A SAMPLE, not a proof: 8 pages of the ~99 the prepared Glossa queue spans. It is enough to stop a blanket plate read, not enough to write 'this volume has none' into a work page.
findings.consequence: Do NOT commission the ~99-page read for the Glossa block. Spot-check 1-2 pages per book at chunking; record tier 2 with this reason where the check is clean.
findings.also: archive.org's Google OCR does not carry the apparatus either, and this was tested rather than assumed: patrologiaecurs139unkngoog_djvu.txt (PL 202, the volume whose notes we HAVE) holds 35 instances of 'Forte' in the whole volume, every one of them the ordinary adverb inside the body text, while work 11613 alone carries ~60 real foot-of-page notes. The OCR is not a cheap detector for this layer.
